title: TCA, FormEngine, and Backend Forms
hints: TCA changes can affect persisted data, editor workflows, and generated backend forms.
Prefer established TCA option names and existing FormEngine behavior.
Add functional coverage for TCA processing, data providers, or backend form rendering behavior.

A new field or option is user-facing, so it needs its labels in the same change — the field label, and the item labels of a select. An unlabelled field renders its own key to the editor. typo3_label_lookup says which trans-units the installation already has.

hints.text: typo3/sysext/core/Classes/Schema/ is the typed API over TCA. Ask TcaSchemaFactory for a TcaSchema and query it — fields, capabilities, relations, labels — instead of reading $GLOBALS['TCA'] directly.
A patch that reads TCA is increasingly expected to go through the schema rather than through the array; new code that touches record structure should not add a fresh $GLOBALS['TCA'] access.
The schema is cached per package set, so a change to how it is built is a functional-test change, not a unit-test one.

title: FormEngine Data Providers
hints: FormEngine assembles its data through providers registered per form data group in $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['SYS']['formEngine']['formDataGroup']. The core declares the defaults in typo3/sysext/core/Configuration/DefaultConfiguration.php, but extensions add to them, so which groups and providers your installation really has is what typo3_configuration_lookup with path SYS/formEngine/formDataGroup answers.

Each provider maps to an array with 'depends' and 'before', both listing other provider classes. That graph is what orders the run, not the order the entries are written in — so the fix for a provider that sees stale data is usually an added dependency, not a change inside the provider class.
A provider that reads merged page TSconfig has to depend on PageTsConfigMerged, or it runs before the TSconfig it reads has been merged.
DefaultConfiguration.php is the default of TYPO3_CONF_VARS: an edit there changes behaviour in every installation, so say what changed and why in the patch description.
Registering or reordering a provider is a runtime-configuration change. It is covered by a functional test that renders the form data, not by a unit test of the provider in isolation.

title: What a Datetime Column Stores, and When It Is Null

hints.text: A TCA type=datetime field that is not nullable never holds SQL NULL. QueryHelper::transformDateTimeToDatabaseValue() writes 0 for an integer column and the empty literal for a native one — '0000-00-00' for dbType=date, '0000-00-00 00:00:00' for datetime, '00:00:00' for time.

DateTimeFactory::fromDatabase() maps that same empty value back to null on read. So a mapped property reading null does not mean the column is NULL, and a query for IS NULL does not find the row the object came from. That asymmetry is what a report of a query not finding its own object turns out to be.

Which value counts as empty depends on the column: for a non-nullable field it is the native literal where a dbType is set and 0 otherwise. A nullable native column additionally reads the legacy '0000-00-00' literal back as null, because rows written before it was nullable still carry it.

nullable defaults to false. DateTimeFieldType::isNullable() overrides that to true where a dbType is set, so a native date, datetime or time column is nullable unless the TCA says otherwise, while an integer column is not.
Before that override existed, DateTimeFieldType inherited isNullable() and the default was false for a native column as well.

Extbase omits a null property from the INSERT rather than writing NULL — Backend::insertObject() only fills a column where the property value is not null — so the column default decides what a new record stores. Reading it back through the factory then yields null again.
